title: How to make a home binder: what goes in and what stays out
intent: Build a small, usable household reference binder with sections, document choices and a practical first page.

findings.evidence: The five named sections include shutoffs, filter sizes, trusted trades, completed jobs and renewal dates; the filled contents table and one-section-at-a-time fallback make this actionable.
findings.fix: Keep the emergency-first sequence and concrete field examples.

findings.evidence: The paper list includes closing documents and the text says the same binder may be handed to a sitter or repair technician. Excluding passwords alone does not protect sensitive financial or ownership paperwork.
findings.fix: Separate a shareable household reference from restricted document storage; use copies or location pointers for sensitive originals.

findings.evidence: The article says digital is impossible to leave behind and an app is the opposite of paper during an outage. These are absolutes, not established capabilities.
findings.fix: Explain device, login, connectivity and offline-copy dependencies; add a dated offline emergency page.

findings.evidence: The setup is detailed, but no owner or review date is assigned to the shutoff/contact pages.
findings.fix: Add last-checked and responsible-person fields, with review after a move, contractor change or system replacement.

suggested_title: How to make a home binder: five sections and a safe sharing plan
proposed_outline: Start with one emergency reference page

title: Moving into a rental: what to document on day one
intent: Create move-in evidence that supports repair requests and later deposit disputes.

findings.evidence: The four-record system covers dated photos, notice dates, deposit information and written repair reports; it explicitly limits the guide to US rentals and cautions against uninformed rent withholding.
findings.fix: Preserve these scope and escalation boundaries.

findings.evidence: The FAQ says dated photos do the same job as a checklist and are harder to dispute, and that photos and notes hold up regardless of local rules. California DRE recommends photos in addition to a signed checklist, not as a guaranteed substitute.
findings.fix: Say photos supplement the inventory; request signatures, retain copies and comply with local submission deadlines. Remove guarantees about evidentiary outcomes.

findings.evidence: The summary promises four records settle most deposit arguments. No outcome data supports 'most'; the text itself recognizes local legal variation.
findings.fix: Use 'help document and challenge deductions' rather than a promised dispute outcome.

findings.evidence: The day-one record omits file names, submission date/receipt, landlord acknowledgement, key count and meter readings.
findings.fix: Add a room-by-room record with original-file backup and a ready-to-send condition email; keep acknowledgement separate from agreement.

suggested_title: Rental move-in checklist: photos, signed condition records and deposit paperwork

title: Debt snowball vs avalanche: which costs less, which sticks
intent: Compare repayment order, interest and motivation using the reader's own debts.

findings.evidence: Three debts are fully specified; extra-payment sensitivity, a wider-rate-gap example, promotional-rate limits and constant-minimum assumptions go well beyond definitions.
findings.fix: Retain the worked comparisons and explicit model boundaries.

findings.evidence: 'Why the gap is often small' generalizes from the selected example. CFPB explains the methods but does not establish how commonly savings are small.
findings.fix: Rename to 'Why the gap is small in this example'; avoid population-level claims without evidence.

findings.evidence: The recommendation chooses snowball for a $114 gap and avalanche for hundreds, without establishing that the reader would abandon avalanche or can absorb that cost.
findings.fix: Present the dollar tradeoff neutrally and let the reader weigh motivation, liquidity and cost; label the threshold as editorial preference, not a rule.

findings.evidence: The FAQ asserts steady $100 helps more than $400 in one month and nothing the next; these are unequal totals over the stated period, and timing also affects interest.
findings.fix: Compare equal cumulative contributions over the same time horizon and distinguish sustainability from mathematical savings.

findings.evidence: Independent APR/12 calculation closely reproduced the $200 totals within cents but the text does not specify first-payment month, rounding or whether snowball order stays fixed. Re-sorting balances changes the $0 path.
findings.fix: Publish a reproducible payment schedule and declare ordering, rounding, leftover allocation and first-payment date before treating exact cents/dates as verified.

suggested_title: Debt snowball vs avalanche: compare interest, payoff milestones and monthly relief

findings.evidence: The $1,668 monthly-only and $223 non-monthly amounts correctly total $1,891; weekly and fortnightly conversions avoid the common four-week-month error.

findings.evidence: The introduction says subscriptions are excluded, yet streaming and an annual gym membership appear in the worked total; the FAQ allows either arrangement.

title: How to organize your finances when everything is scattered
intent: Get an overwhelmed reader from scattered information to one provisional money overview and a manageable verification step.

findings.evidence: The six-area example shows real uncertainty markers for electric, insurance, balances and APR rather than invented precision; the ten-minute sequence turns each gap into an errand.
findings.fix: Keep the memory-first approach as a clearly provisional intake.

findings.evidence: The Goals row gives $5,000 by next summer and says 'None yet' under gap to close, despite omitting current earmarked savings and an exact date.
findings.fix: Mark those goal inputs unknown too; show remaining amount and deadline before planning contributions.

findings.evidence: Readers choose safe-to-spend or debt payoff at minute seven, then close only one gap; approximate balances are not a verified spending allowance.
findings.fix: Add a clear stop gate: verify current balances, pending transactions and obligations through the relevant payday before acting on a spending figure.

findings.evidence: The tax retention shorthand says three years from filing, while IRS says early-filed returns count from the due date and lists longer exceptions.
findings.fix: Keep this section short but add early-filing treatment and link readers to the IRS exceptions before discarding anything.

title: How to split bills with a partner or roommate: 3 methods
intent: Choose and calculate an agreed household cost split and make settlement predictable.

findings.evidence: The $4,200/$2,100 example compares equal versus proportional burdens, and scripts cover privacy and changed income. The lease-liability caveat prevents mistaking a private split for a landlord agreement.
findings.fix: Retain the worked fairness comparison and scripts.

findings.evidence: The table uses exact two-thirds ($1,328 of $1,992), but instructions and product entry use 67 percent, which yields $1,334.64, a $6.64 difference.
findings.fix: Keep full ratios through calculation and round only final cents, or consistently show the agreed 67/33 amounts and explain the difference.

findings.evidence: The subtitle promises equal, income or room; the three-method table instead uses equal, income or item. Room-size is effectively a fourth method.
findings.fix: Make labels consistent or explicitly frame room weighting as a roommate-specific variant.

findings.evidence: Room rent allocates the entire $2,700 solely by bedroom area, without distinguishing equally shared common space. It is an agreement option, not uniquely fair.
findings.fix: Label it one possible convention and offer an optional equal common-space portion plus weighted private-space portion.

findings.evidence: Joint-account suitability is discussed but access/withdrawal risks and account closure are not.
findings.fix: Add a bank-terms check and a brief exit agreement without implying a joint account is required.

proposed_outline: Compare equal and exact income ratios

title: Subscription tracker: the six fields that catch renewals
intent: Track known subscriptions so renewal decisions happen before a charge and cancellations can be confirmed.

findings.evidence: The five-row example differentiates annual renewals, shared cost and decision status; the guide distinguishes finding subscriptions from tracking or canceling them.
findings.fix: Keep this narrower scope and the account-page verification step.

findings.evidence: Both opening and FAQ call renewal date the last day to cancel, while the trial FAQ itself admits earlier processing constraints.
findings.fix: Track the provider's actual cancellation cutoff separately from charge date; set reminders before the cutoff and verify terms, rather than treating renewal day as safe.

findings.evidence: A monthly review looks ahead only two weeks. Without correctly installed per-item reminders, renewals in the later half of the interval are missed.
findings.fix: Look through the next scheduled review plus a buffer, or review weekly; make reminder setup an explicit completed step.

findings.evidence: The checklist says remove canceled items, yet the article also advises retaining cancellation requests and checking stopped charges.
findings.fix: Archive canceled rows with request date, confirmation reference and last verification instead of deleting them.

findings.evidence: The six fields do not record billing channel or management link, so an Apple/Google/direct subscription can be harder to cancel even with a date.
findings.fix: Add optional billing channel, account owner and cancellation link without storing credentials.

suggested_title: Subscription tracker: renewal dates, cancellation deadlines and proof
